annotation.interpretation_a: A frame payload can terminate *anywhere* before the end of the identified fields, even if it's only a single byte short.
annotation.interpretation_b: A frame payload must contain *all* of the identified fields, and terminating before the end implies a more severe error than simply being short a few bytes.
annotation.justification: The phrase 'before the end of the identified fields' is insufficiently precise. It's unclear whether a frame terminating mid-way through the last field is treated the same as a frame terminating after only a few bytes of the first field. This affects how an implementation would handle partial reads and error detection.
annotation.missing_information: The granularity of 'before the end' is not specified. Does this apply to any partial field, or only to the last field?
